claim: Candidate B of the ADR-0012 decision spike (a provider-enforced publication firewall over STOCK crates.io slatedb 0.15.0, fresh credential domain per authority rotation) is implemented, its qualifying matrix passes (4/4), and the mutant that removes the firewall gate is killed by both fencing cases. With this, BOTH candidates of the directive's two-candidate spike (J.3/D4, AC-FORK-SPIKE) are built and measured.
status: candidate implemented and measured - NOT the normative decision; comparison recorded in ADR-0012
directive_item: F4/F5 OPEN-P0; directive J.3/D4 (AC-FORK-SPIKE); NEXT-SESSION follow-up 4
crate: spikes/publication-firewall (workspace-external, publish = false, nothing links it)

base.version: 0.15.0 (exact pin, crates.io, UNPATCHED - that is the point of this candidate)

mechanism.shape: ObjectStore wrapper (FirewalledStore) bound to a per-handle credential domain; a PublicationAuthority cell (the controller stand-in / provider-credential model) names the currently authorized domain; every MUTATION of a publication path (any path with a 'manifest' segment) is admitted only when handle domain == authorized domain; reads and data-path writes (SSTs) always pass - a revoked writer can at worst strand orphan bytes.
mechanism.provider_mapping: in production the same predicate is enforced server-side by scoped credentials (R2 API tokens / IAM session credentials) that the controller rotates; the spike enforces it in-process so semantics are measurable offline

cases: every_publication_path_flows_through_the_firewall (coverage: a full open/put/flush/close cycle's manifest publications are all firewall-visible and path-identifiable; data writes are distinguishable)

a_revoked_writer_cannot_publish_and_a_successor_can (SL-P1 pause-fence-resume: rotation alone fences the stale flush at the store boundary, successor opens and publishes, predecessor's durable prefix intact, refusals are manifest-path-only)
a_stale_reopen_is_refused_at_open (the directive's stale-reopen case: open itself publishes, so a revoked domain cannot reacquire a writer)
the_firewall_vocabulary_has_no_epoch_in_it (the measured structural LIMIT, as an executable fact: the firewall observes paths/opaque bytes only)

executed.mutant: the domain gate removed from FirewalledStore::admit (allowed = true)
executed.result: test result: FAILED. 2 passed; 2 failed - a_revoked_writer_cannot_publish_and_a_successor_can FAILED, a_stale_reopen_is_refused_at_open FAILED

measured_findings.coverage_advantage_over_upstream_fencing: the firewall sits on the ONLY channel to storage, so it gates every publication path including the Admin/StoredManifest checkpoint paths that bypass upstream's FenceableManifest fencing types entirely - Candidate A has to patch those paths one by one.
measured_findings.q13_interaction_observed: first run HUNG: with the stock default object_store_max_retries: None ('retry transient errors indefinitely'), the firewall's refusal put flush() into an infinite retry loop - the fenced writer hung instead of failing. Candidate B inherits this hazard on every refusal path and requires the bounded-retry posture (Some(n)) to fail closed; Candidate A's typed Fenced error is terminal by construction. This was a real defect in the spike's first posture() and is recorded, not hidden.
measured_findings.failure_surface: the stale writer observes an opaque object_store::Error::Generic surfaced through whatever operation happened to publish (flush, open) - not a typed fenced outcome. Upstream cannot distinguish 'fenced' from 'store outage', so its retry/recovery classification treats fencing as infrastructure failure.
measured_findings.inv_78_80_not_satisfiable: the firewall decides WHO may publish but the epoch NUMBERS inside manifests remain internally allocated by stock SlateDB; no wrapper of this shape can make publications carry controller-minted SlateWriterEpoch/SlateCompactorEpoch values, and adopting the store's own numbering is the prohibited observe-and-bind. This is a structural gap of Candidate B, permanent at any wrapper thickness.
measured_findings.granularity: fencing is per credential domain (per handle), not per (writer, compactor) epoch pair; separating writer from compactor authority requires distinct domains, which the provider credential model supports but the spike models with a single cell.

comparison_inputs_for_adr_0012.candidate_a: exact external epochs on every publication (inv. 78-80 satisfied), typed Fenced outcomes, ~90 non-test patch lines over the digest-pinned crate, fork maintenance cost, patches upstreamable
comparison_inputs_for_adr_0012.candidate_b: zero fork cost, total path coverage including Admin, provider-enforceable server-side (defense in depth even if the process is compromised), but inv. 78-80 unsatisfiable, opaque failure surface, and fail-closed only under a bounded-retry posture
comparison_inputs_for_adr_0012.note: the candidates COMPOSE: B's provider-enforced credential rotation is defense-in-depth underneath A's exact epochs, and nothing in A precludes deploying B's credential model as the storage-side backstop. The decision recorded in ADR-0012 weighs A as the fencing mechanism of record with B's credential rotation as the platform backstop, NOT an either/or.
